title: The Indus Waters Treaty was put in abeyance on 23 April 2025, and the word abeyance appears nowhere in the treaty, whose only exit is a duly ratified treaty concluded by both Governments
summary: Following the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025, in which 26 people were killed, the Cabinet Committee on Security decided that the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 "will be held in abeyance with immediate effect, until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism". The same decision closed the Integrated Check Post at Attari, suspended bilateral trade, and excluded Pakistani nationals from the SAARC Visa Exemption Scheme. The treaty's own final provisions, Article XII, provide two mechanisms and no others: modification "by a duly ratified treaty concluded for that purpose between the two Governments", and continuation in force "until terminated by a duly ratified treaty concluded for that purpose between the two Governments".
claimAtLaunch: A stated condition rather than a stated outcome: the treaty is held in abeyance until Pakistan "credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism". The Press Information Bureau's account frames the measure as severing an economic lifeline without escalating direct military conflict, and quotes the formulation "Blood and water cannot flow together".
whatHappened: THE TREATY CONTAINS NO MECHANISM ANSWERING TO WHAT WAS DONE, AND THIS IS CHECKABLE RATHER THAN ARGUABLE. Across the full text and all annexures — 215,794 characters — the words abeyance, suspension, termination and denounce do not appear at all. The word terminated appears once, in Article XII(4), and requires a duly ratified treaty concluded by both Governments. The two occurrences of suspend are the arbitral Court suspending its own proceedings pending replacement of an arbitrator under Annexure G, and the three occurrences of withdraw are withdrawals of water from named tributaries. COMMITMENT STATE (a), WITH A TRIGGER THAT NAMES NO TEST. The condition for reversal is an assessment of another state's conduct — credibly and irrevocably abjuring support for cross-border terrorism — and nothing published states who judges it, against what criterion, or on what evidence.
assessmentNote: The action itself is established and in effect, and its instrument-side facts are now fully checkable. What cannot be scored is whether it achieves its stated end, because the end names no evaluator and no test: a condition that only one party assesses, by criteria it has not published, cannot be shown to be met or unmet at any future date. This record does NOT adjudicate the treaty-law question. Whether abeyance is available to a party outside the treaty's own terms is a question for bodies whose material could not be retrieved here, and the record confines itself to what the treaty says and what the decision says.
caseFor: A state that believes it is being attacked from across a border is not obliged to keep every instrument of cooperation running unchanged, and the treaty is among the very few points of leverage India holds that does not require force. The measure was calibrated to that: the Press Information Bureau's account presents it explicitly as pressure applied without escalating direct military conflict, which is the choice most likely to avoid deaths. The condition attached is a condition for RESTORATION, not a demand for territory or payment — the treaty returns if the conduct stops — and stating a reversal condition at all is more than a purely punitive measure would have offered. The treaty has also survived three wars and been administered continuously since 1960, which is the strongest argument that India has treated it as durable rather than disposable, and makes the departure a considered one rather than a reflex.
caseAgainst: The instrument's own terms provide exactly two routes, modification and termination, and both require the agreement of both Governments; the treaty offers no unilateral exit and no intermediate state, and a checked search of its full text finds no vocabulary for one. The government's own account does not settle which act it performed: one sentence describes "India's termination of the Indus Waters Treaty" and the next says the treaty "will be held in abeyance", and termination and abeyance are not the same legal act. The treaty is also expressly limited by Article XI(1)(a) to rights and obligations concerning the use of the waters and matters incidental thereto, while the condition attached to its abeyance concerns conduct outside that subject entirely. And a reversal condition assessed by one party alone, against criteria it has not published, is indistinguishable in operation from an indefinite one.

unmeasured.what: India's stated legal basis for placing the treaty in abeyance
unmeasured.why: The measure was announced as a decision. Nothing retrieved states the provision, doctrine or instrument relied upon, and the treaty's own text supplies no mechanism of that name. This is recorded as absent from what was retrieved, not as non-existent — a legal position may have been stated in material this run could not reach, and the Permanent Court of Arbitration's site refused two independent clients with HTTP 403.
unmeasured.wouldFill: A Ministry of External Affairs or Ministry of Law statement of the legal basis, a Parliamentary answer, or India's filings in any proceeding on the question.

unmeasured.what: Who determines whether Pakistan has "credibly and irrevocably" abjured support for cross-border terrorism, and by what test
unmeasured.why: The condition is the sole stated route back to the treaty's operation, and no evaluator, criterion, evidentiary standard or review point appears in anything retrieved. Without one the condition cannot be shown to be satisfied, which means the abeyance cannot be shown to have ended or to have failed to end.
unmeasured.wouldFill: Any published criterion, review mechanism or periodic assessment attached to the decision.

unmeasured.what: What has changed in the actual operation of the treaty since 23 April 2025 — data sharing, Permanent Indus Commission meetings, or flows
unmeasured.why: Abeyance is a status; what it altered in practice is a separate question. Nothing retrieved states whether Commission meetings ceased, whether hydrological data transmission stopped, or whether any physical flow changed.
unmeasured.wouldFill: A Ministry of Jal Shakti or Permanent Indus Commission statement, or a Parliamentary answer on the treaty's operation since the decision.

caveat: The zero counts above are from the treaty's own full text as registered with the United Nations, which is the natural place for its exit provisions and covers the whole instrument; they are a checked absence, not a failed search. THE NON-ZERO COUNTS WERE READ BEFORE THEY WERE USED, and this matters: `suspend` returns two hits and `withdraw` three, and banked as counts they would have supported the opposite conclusion — both `suspend` hits are the arbitral Court pausing its own proceedings, and all three `withdraw` hits are withdrawals of water. The figures the Press Information Bureau gives for Pakistan's dependence on the Indus system — 80 per cent of 16 million hectares of agricultural land, 93 per cent of total water use, 237 million people, one-fourth of GDP — are reproduced here as that document's claims about another country, with no basis, method or source stated in it, and are not adopted by this record. The Permanent Court of Arbitration proceedings are not covered: `pca-cpa.org` and `pcacases.com` both returned HTTP 403 to independent requests, so nothing about them is asserted either way.

title: The trade suspended on 23 April 2025 was already one-directional and the two governments do not agree what it was: for 2024 India reports US$1,183.10m of exports to Pakistan against Pakistan's US$304.93m of imports from India
summary: The Cabinet Committee on Security decision of 23 April 2025 closed the Integrated Check Post at Attari with immediate effect, requiring those who had crossed with valid endorsements to return by 1 May 2025, and suspended all bilateral trade with Pakistan. UN Comtrade, on India's own returns, gives India's exports to Pakistan as US$523.22m in 2023, US$1,183.10m in 2024 and US$352.27m in 2025, against imports from Pakistan of US$7.69m, US$6.42m and US$3.73m in the same years. Pakistan's returns for the same trade are far smaller: imports from India of US$258.20m, US$304.93m and US$311.31m, and exports to India of US$0.04m, US$0.02m and US$0.11m.
claimAtLaunch: No target, value or duration is announced. The measure is presented by the Press Information Bureau as severing an economic lifeline without escalating direct military conflict, alongside the Indus Waters Treaty abeyance recorded at L-0216, and is described as halting exports of goods including onions and banning imports of cement and textiles.
whatHappened: THE FLOW SUSPENDED WAS ALREADY ALMOST ENTIRELY ONE-WAY. On India's own figures for 2024, exports to Pakistan of US$1,183.10m stood against imports from Pakistan of US$6.42m — India sent about 184 times what it received, so a suspension of "all bilateral trade" removes an Indian export market and almost nothing on the import side. THE TWO GOVERNMENTS DISAGREE ABOUT THE SIZE OF THAT MARKET BY MULTIPLES. For 2024 India reports US$1,183.10m of exports to Pakistan while Pakistan reports US$304.93m of imports from India — a gap of US$878.17m, with India's figure 3.88 times Pakistan's. The same disagreement runs the other way and is larger in ratio: for 2024 India records US$6.42m of imports from Pakistan against Pakistan's US$0.02m of exports to India. THE EFFECT OF THE SUSPENSION IS NOT MEASURED HERE. The 2025 annual figures straddle 23 April, and no monthly series for India is available on this route, so the year cannot be split into its pre- and post-decision parts.
assessmentNote: The decision announces no target, no value and no duration, so there is nothing that could have worked or failed. What this record establishes is the measurement position: what the suspended trade was on each side's account, that the two accounts differ by multiples, and that the suspension's own effect cannot be isolated from the series available. Deliberately NOT scored as an outcome — a fall in the 2025 annual figure is consistent with the suspension and also with a return from an exceptional 2024, and nothing retrieved separates them.
caseFor: As economic coercion goes this is unusually low-cost to the party imposing it, and that is a real argument in its favour rather than a criticism. India was the seller in this relationship by a factor of roughly 184 to one on its own 2024 figures, so suspending the trade forgoes an export market while surrendering almost no import dependence — there is no supply Indian industry loses. Closing a single land crossing at Attari is also the most reversible of the measures announced that day: an Integrated Check Post can be reopened by the same decision that closed it, unlike a treaty. And the government stated what it was doing in specific terms, naming affected goods on both sides, which is more than a general announcement of economic measures would have offered.
caseAgainst: A government suspending a trade should be able to say how large it was, and here the two parties' figures differ by more than the whole of the smaller one — for 2024 the gap is US$878.17m against Pakistan's stated US$304.93m. Whichever figure a reader takes, the other is wrong by a margin that dwarfs any plausible valuation adjustment, and no Indian document retrieved acknowledges the divergence or explains it. The asymmetry also cuts against the framing: describing the measure as severing an economic lifeline is a claim about the effect on Pakistan, and the numbers that would support it are the numbers in dispute. And the one thing that would show whether the suspension bit — a monthly series across April 2025 — is not published on this route, so the measure's effect is unavailable at exactly the moment it matters.
differentFactsNote: Both instruments measure the same quantity — trade between India and Pakistan in a given year — and disagree by multiples in both directions and in every year checked. Neither figure is adopted and no midpoint is taken. Ordinary explanations exist for a divergence of this kind, including valuation convention between export and import records and attribution of goods routed through third countries, and none is asserted here because no retrieved source states which applies or in what proportion. This is the same shape as the India-China pair at P-119 and larger: there the ratio is a fraction, here India's 2024 export figure is 3.88 times Pakistan's import figure. The gap is arithmetically computable and its magnitude is stated — US$878.17m for 2024 — but it is not treated as a measured quantity, because it is the difference between two accounts of the same trade rather than anything either party reports. Which side is short, and by how much, is exactly what is unresolved.

unmeasured.why: The annual figures span the decision date. A monthly series would isolate the trade before and after 23 April 2025 and is the only thing that would make the suspension's effect measurable; UN Comtrade's public preview returns no monthly rows for India on this query.
unmeasured.wouldFill: A monthly Comtrade series, or Department of Commerce monthly trade data for Pakistan as a partner.

unmeasured.what: Which of the two national accounts of the trade is closer to correct, and why they diverge
unmeasured.why: The divergence is present in every year checked, runs in both directions, and reaches 3.88 times on India's 2024 exports. Nothing retrieved from either government acknowledges it or states a cause, so no basis exists for preferring one series or reconciling them.
unmeasured.wouldFill: A reconciliation by either statistical authority, or a Comtrade partner-attribution note covering India-Pakistan trade.

unmeasured.what: The value of trade actually forgone since the suspension, and whether goods continue to reach Pakistan through third countries
unmeasured.why: The decision suspends direct bilateral trade. Whether the goods it covered ceased to move or were re-routed is a different question from whether direct trade fell, and nothing retrieved addresses it.
unmeasured.wouldFill: A Department of Commerce assessment of the suspension's effect, or third-country trade data showing a corresponding rise.

THEY ARE NOT USED TO MEASURE THE SUSPENSION: the year straddles 23 April, no monthly series is available, and this record does not report the fall from 2024 as an effect of the decision. It also does not establish that the 2025 figures are complete years — the source carries no completeness indicator on this route, and a partial year would understate both sides. The ratio of about 184 to one is India's 2024 exports to Pakistan divided by India's 2024 imports from Pakistan, both from India's own returns in the same year and the same dataset, so it compares like with like; no ratio is formed across the two reporters. All figures are UN Comtrade annual, commodity code TOTAL, in current US dollars.

title: Four Indian government publication channels cannot be read by an ordinary client, and in every case but one the documents survive only because a different arm of the same government republishes them
summary: Every retrieval blockage recorded during phase 14 was re-tested by varying the host. Four Indian government channels remain unreadable: the Ministry of External Affairs website, which returns HTTP 200 and a JavaScript scaffold with no document text; the Ministry of Defence and Department of Defence Production sites, whose HTTPS connections fail outright; and the e-Gazette, unreachable on both of its hosts. In three of the four cases the material itself proved fully retrievable elsewhere — through the Press Information Bureau for ministry documents, and through the United Nations Treaty Series for a treaty that the Ministry's own portal serves only as an image. For the e-Gazette no alternate route was found.
claimAtLaunch: No commitment is under test here. Every one of these sites is an official publication channel and is presented as the route by which the relevant documents are made public; that is the only claim involved, and it is implicit in their existence rather than announced.
whatHappened: THE BLOCKAGE IS AT THE MINISTRY'S OWN WEBSITE, AND THE RECORD SURVIVES BECAUSE A DIFFERENT ARM REPUBLISHES IT. mea.gov.in returns HTTP 200 with 82,719 bytes on its press-releases path, of which 4,326 characters are navigation chrome carrying the string "Loading..." and no release text; the same failure was confirmed earlier on its media-briefings path. mod.gov.in and ddpmod.gov.in do not complete an HTTPS connection at all. egazette.gov.in and egazette.nic.in both fail to connect. Against this, the Press Information Bureau served a Ministry of Defence document of 1,994,703 bytes on request, and has carried Power, Home Affairs, Commerce and Prime Minister's Office material throughout this phase; and the Indus Waters Treaty — a 5MB image scan yielding 113 bytes of text on the Ministry's own legal-treaties portal — is a 215,794-character machine-readable document in the United Nations Treaty Series, where India registered it in 1962. ARCHIVING DOES NOT RESCUE A JAVASCRIPT SHELL. The Internet Archive's snapshot of the same Ministry page returns 4,326 characters, still carrying "Loading..." and still containing no release text: the crawler captured the scaffold, because the scaffold is what the server sends.
assessmentNote: No target for the accessibility of the public record is announced by any of these bodies, so there is nothing that could have worked or failed. What this record establishes is a measurement precondition for everything else in the corpus: which official channels can be read, which cannot, and — the part that matters — that a failure to read a ministry's website is not evidence that its documents are unpublished. Recorded because the opposite inference was made three times in this phase and was wrong each time.
caseFor: The public record is more robust than any single channel's failure suggests, and that is the honest headline. Every ministry document sought during this phase was obtained, because the Press Information Bureau republishes across ministries and does so as server-rendered pages an ordinary client can read; the redundancy is real and it worked. For treaties the redundancy extends outside the government entirely — registration with the United Nations produced a machine-readable text of a 1960 instrument that the responsible ministry serves only as an image, which is the international registration system doing exactly what it exists for. A ministry website being slow, broken or JavaScript-heavy is also an ordinary technical condition rather than a policy of concealment, and nothing here suggests otherwise.
caseAgainst: A publication channel that cannot be read is not publishing, whatever it intends. Three of these are the designated route to their own material, and a citizen with a standard client gets HTTP 200 and an empty page from the Ministry of External Affairs — the failure mode that looks most like success and is hardest to distinguish from an absence. The redundancy that rescues the record is also incidental rather than designed: the Press Information Bureau carries what it carries, and a document no press release covers has no second route. The e-Gazette is the case that proves it, being both unreachable and unduplicated — it is the channel of legal record, and nothing else republishes it. And an archived copy of a JavaScript scaffold means the failure is being preserved rather than the document, so the loss is not merely current.

unmeasured.what: How much Ministry of External Affairs material has no Press Information Bureau equivalent
unmeasured.why: The redundancy that rescued this phase is opportunistic. Establishing its coverage would require enumerating what the Ministry publishes, which is precisely what cannot be read from the blocked channel. The gap is unmeasurable from the outside for the same reason it matters.
unmeasured.wouldFill: A server-rendered index or a machine-readable feed from the Ministry, either of which would make its output enumerable.

unmeasured.what: Whether these channels are readable from other networks, clients or jurisdictions
unmeasured.why: Every test here ran from one location. A connection failure is a relationship between a client and a server, and this record states what one client observed rather than asserting a property of the servers. Two hosts were tried for the e-Gazette and for the arbitration site, and the Ministry site was tried on two paths, two dates and through the Internet Archive — but that is host variation, not network variation.
unmeasured.wouldFill: The same requests from an independent network, or a public status or uptime record for the sites.

caveat: This record states what one client observed on 5 August 2026 and on the earlier dates noted in the verification log; it does not assert that these sites are unreachable in general, and the second unmeasured says so. The Permanent Court of Arbitration is deliberately excluded from the four: it returned HTTP 403 from both pca-cpa.org and pcacases.com and its Internet Archive snapshot resolves to the case index rather than the case, but it is not an Indian government publication channel and belongs to a different question. The 4,326-character figure is the normalised text remaining after markup is stripped, not the byte size served, and the two differ by more than an order of magnitude — which is the point: the byte size looks like a document and the text is not one.
